elements.problem: Low risk rule is a conjunction of 'no' on eight findings. Page low risk = no current thoughts AND (no recent history OR not agitated). Rule additionally excludes agitation even when no history, so a calm-history-free agitated patient is neither high nor low risk (page: No on history -> low). Minor divergence. Also absence of data makes 'no' true, risking low-risk on empty record.

rule_level_problems.problem: Triggers on any 'Thoughts of self harm' finding regardless of timing or current status; the page makes Urgent only for attempt or high risk. Also current thoughts/plans reach Urgent only through the high-risk diagnosis, relying on a derived active_condition.

Contains both qualified and unqualified Planning suicide, and Suicidal thoughts with and without Current inside the task trigger; duplicate/overlapping items. Thoughts of self harm in the trigger is not in check_for, and Suicide attempt/Intentionally harming self are not in check_for.
Defined by absence of eight findings; empty record yields low risk. Excludes agitation even when history absent, diverging from page branch (no history -> low risk).
Past-year acts are mapped to history 'situation' concepts rather than acute event findings; attempted self-harm itself does not produce high risk (only Urgent).

summary: The core page logic (current thoughts/plans, recent history combined with agitation, low risk) is encoded in a high-risk and a low-risk probable diagnosis plus an Urgent priority. Most consequential problems: the Urgent priority fires on any Thoughts of self harm (not justified by the page) and the low-risk rule uses absence of findings, diverging from the page's branch and succeeding on empty data. Management steps and flowchart labels are out of scope.
